note: In the Gospel accounts Jesus flips the money-changers' tables in the temple. The bar uses that image for a monetary order: the tables where currency gets exchanged are turned over, not talked into a better fee.
Bankster stitches banker and gangster. In sound-money slang it is the credit system treated as a racket — the crowd the previous line says someone finally crossed.

Satoshi Nakamoto published Bitcoin in 2008 and stopped writing publicly in 2011. The identity was never proven. The question is the standing one, and the next line is for the people who keep volunteering to answer it.

phrase: Those who claim to be are posers
note: A long list of people have said they are Satoshi, or have had the claim hung on them. None has shown the genesis keys. Poser is the claimant without that proof.

Cyber hornets is Michael Saylor's name for bitcoiners who swarm to defend the network and the culture around it. The "plan b" in the same bar is the backup that swarm is supposed to carry if the old institutions will not.
New units of fiat dilute the ones people already hold. Calling that corrosive is the hard-money claim: inflation is not a neutral dial. It eats savings.

phrase: prop that GDP up with explosives
note: GDP counts spending, including debt-funded stimulus and war. The picture is an economy whose headline growth is held up by blowing things up — activity in the accounts, destruction underneath.

Gresham's law: when two monies are both legal tender, the worse one gets spent and the better one gets hoarded. People pass along what is losing value and keep what is scarce. The lyric spells it in lowercase and treats the habit as survival.

Not the names of songs. In Bitcoin circles Jack Kruse — a neurosurgeon, often misspelled Cruze — uses "titles" for legal title: deeds and other paper claims on property. That framing has come up in his conversations with Robert Breedlove. The hook hits the word, then turns to the old order and a revival.
The old, in this chorus, is the paper regime those titles belong to. The line is a burial. The revival comes next.
After "breathe new life," the chorus names the mood. A revival is the old thing waking in a new form — here, money with a cap and with keys, set against the system the verse just attacked.

Diamond hands means refusing to sell through a drawdown. Laser eyes were the 2021 profile-picture badge aimed at a bitcoin price of $100,000. One line makes the holder and the meme the same costume, worn across tribes.
"We're so early" is the adoption claim that the position is still early even after a large price move. "That's for surely" is the rhyme under it, not a price target.
Entreprises is the French spelling. The bar means enterprises: companies and institutions finally showing up. "While it's ripe" is the tell — they want in once the move is obvious.
A committee, a board, a compliance desk. The institutions in the surrounding lines cannot just buy. Someone has to sign. That lag is what "late" looks like.
A slice is a piece of the upside cut after the fact. The late allocator arrives once early holders have already stacked, and asks for a share.

phrase: I see jack do all this good abroad
note: Read with the El Salvador line, jack is Jack Mallers. At Bitcoin 2021 in Miami he presented that country's plan to make bitcoin legal tender, and Strike's work was tied to the rollout. "Abroad" is that nation-state chapter.
In 2021 Nayib Bukele's government made bitcoin legal tender, the first nation-state to do so. The line is that adoption: bitcoin taken onto a country's books, not used as a metaphor.
Fiat is state currency by decree. Leaving it at the door means the room on the other side settles in bitcoin. The decree stays outside.
The fight in the song is monetary and memetic. Opting out, holding keys, and letting the harder money win is a war that does not need an army.
Sovereign here means fewer permissions: keys you hold, and — from the El Salvador lines — a country settling off the old correspondent-bank path. The verse is watching that shift unfold.

phrase: Voting with my wealth is my reprisal
note: Reprisal is the payback. The vote is not a ballot. It is where the money sits. You fund the money you trust and withhold it from the one you do not.
